## Summary

The bug was in `app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts:96-99`: `update()` built a raw `Response` with a manual `302` status and `Location` header instead of calling `this.redirect()`. A `302` on a `PUT` request is replayed by the browser/fetch as another `PUT` to the same URL, so the client kept re-hitting `posts.update`, which kept redirecting — an infinite loop (`ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS`), even though the very first update had already saved. Per the project's controller conventions, `this.redirect()` defaults to `303` for non-GET methods precisely so the follow-up request becomes a `GET`, landing on `posts.show`. I replaced the hand-built response with `return this.redirect(\`/posts/${post.id}\`)`, matching the pattern already used in `store()`/`destroy()`. I also added two tests to `tests/PostController.test.ts` covering `posts.update`: one asserting a successful save now returns `303` with `Location: /posts/:id`, and one confirming validation errors still return `422`. `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` both pass (4/4).
